messages:
Priya: @oncall quick heads-up — ACME just opened a support ticket claiming requests were routed to eu-west despite being EU-residency locked. They saw 401s, high latency, and a billing anomaly. They provided an audit alert id: audit_2026_09_12_4578

devops-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT: policy.exception:residency_mismatch for org=acme, request_id=xyz123, routed_region=eu-west-1, home_region=eu-central-1, policy_version=v3.2

Raj: Can you paste the routing decision log and the fallback policy version used? Need the exact route key and node id.

Priya: Pasting the relevant log snippet we got from edge: 
```
2026-09-12T10:11:22Z route_decision: org=acme model=gpt-4x region=eu-central-1 fallback_allowed=true selected=eu-west-1 reason=capacity_pressure
request_id=xyz123 auth_status=401 downstream_host=redwood-edge-eu-west node_id=edge-23
```

Claire: tagging security/compliance. This looks like a data-residency exception. If ACME has regulated data (PII/PHI) this is P0. Who executed the fallback? Need an auditable operator trail + KMS access.

Sam: @Raj disable cross-region fallback for org=acme immediately. Use the admin CLI.

Raj: running now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --org acme --set allow_cross_region_fallback=false --as admin
redwoodctl cache invalidate --org acme routes
```
I got `200 OK` for the route update and cache invalidation queued to canary nodes.

SupportBot: Incident created INC-4567, linked to audit_2026_09_12_4578. Notifying account and legal.

Priya: Customer repro steps they gave: 
1) curl -v -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
2) check response header `x-redwood-region` -> showed `eu-west-1`
3) saw 401 on first request, 200 on retry (token reauth), and billing usage appeared under non-EU ledger for the first call.

Example curl they sent: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

Claire: @security can you pull KMS access logs and operator audit logs for org=acme between 2026-09-12T10:00 and 2026-09-12T10:30? Need key usage + who issued route update calls.

Maya: I'm pinging ACME account rep now. Asking whether the data in question is covered by residency contract (they may have extra clauses).

Sam: Short-term mitigation summary: disabled fallback for ACME, invalidated route caches, and added a strict per-org routing rule. Owner for remediation: @Raj, please produce a postmortem EOD. Also add a 1-min alert for policy.exception:residency_mismatch.

Raj: Created infra tickets INF-7890 (route decision hardening) and INF-7891 (fast path for residency-aware routing). Linking them to INC-4567.

Priya: Sent initial update to ACME support contact; legal looped in. Customer acknowledged the mitigation and asked for detailed timeline.

devops-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: policy.exception cleared for audit_2026_09_12_4578 at 2026-09-12T10:21:00Z (resolution: fallback disabled for org=acme)

Sam: Thanks everyone. Next steps: Raj to lead postmortem + remediation plan, Claire to confirm compliance impact, Maya to coordinate customer comms and any billing credits. We'll dump final notes in #incidents once PM takes the postmortem.
